stumbles.quote: Jev had done well on routing questions, so I was hopeful.
stumbles.why: Refers to earlier Jev work on routing that the text never describes; reader can't tell what 'well' meant or how it relates to this task.
The lint tool is never explained (what it flags, what a 'hit' is), though the whole section depends on it.

stumbles.quote: With the tic's definition from `register.md` in its prompt
stumbles.why: 'The tic' and `register.md` are unexplained; reader doesn't know what a tic is or what the definition says.
Oskar is an unexplained name; his role is unclear.

stumbles.quote: At a 5% error budget it could settle only 24.5%
stumbles.why: 'Settle' and 'error budget' are not defined (what counts as an error, what settling means), so the headline number can't be interpreted.

stumbles.quote: the bar we set in advance was 50%
stumbles.why: Unclear what 50% measures (fraction settled?) and who set it; 'in advance' leans on unstated prior planning.

stumbles.quote: A baseline that knows only the hit's lint category (that category's historical tic rate) reached an AUROC of 0.769.
stumbles.why: Baseline is compared to Jev with definition, but which Jev AUROC (0.808 vs 0.697) the accuracy comparison refers to is unspecified; also 'historical' rate source is unclear.

stumbles.quote: At a 0.5 threshold the baseline beat Jev on accuracy, 0.751 to 0.732.
stumbles.why: Unclear which Jev variant; also sits oddly with the claim that Jev ranked better (0.808 vs 0.769) without explanation.

stumbles.quote: Jev is a small decision model that returns a calibrated probability for a yes/no question in about 160 ms.
stumbles.why: Jev's origin/what 'small' model it is isn't said; also 'public posting review' process is never described.

point: Jev, a small calibrated yes/no model, was rejected for the public posting review because at a 5% error budget it settled only 24.5% of lint hits (bar: 50%), with a simple per-rule baseline performing about as well.
